page.layout: One page of text. At the top, two engraved coin medallions, each with a printed legend around its rim. Below them, one text block of running text in one column, with two paragraphs. Below the text, an ornament (tailpiece) with no text. No margin notes.

main_text.p: OTHO iunior, siue Otho huius nominis secundus, superioris Othonis filius, patri Romanorum Imperatori succedit anno mundi 4935. à Christo nato 973. attamen à patre iam ante sex annos fuerat Imperator creatus: cuius etiam opera Saracenos, Græcósque Calabria expulerat. Hic mortuo patre Henricum Bauariæ Ducem nouis rebus studentem, debellauit: atque aduersus Lotarium Francorum Regem, qui sibi Lotaringiam asserebat, Galliam ingressus, fœdis populationibus eam vastauit. At dum reuertitur, in Axonæ fluuii transitu graui incommodo à Fracis[?] afficitur, quibusdam ex suis militibus vorticibus absorptis, pluribus ab insequente hoste interfectis. Dum in Italiam festinat ad famam Græcorum principum, qui Saraceno etiam milite instructi Italiam sibi vendicabant, vincitur: ac scapha confcensa, à piratis captus, in Siciliam ducitur: liberatus, omnem in Beneuentanos iram, quòd signa deseruissent, effundit: ciuitatem capit, spoliat, incendit. Tandem fato concessit, cum imperasset solus post patrem annos decem. Consulito Blond. lib. 3. Deca. 2. Egna lib. 3. Ab. Vrfper.
THEOPHANIA uxor huius Othonis secundi filia fuit Nicephori Græcorum Imperatoris, quem regno pulsum, restituit, & confirmauit Otho. Vide Sup. Chro. lib. 12.

page.notes: The coin legends are printed within the engravings; the right legend's first word is uncertain on the scan. The ornament below the text is a decorative tailpiece with no text. Faint marks in the right margin near the lower text are show-through from the other side and were left out. The word "Fracis" is uncertain: it may carry an accent. Some words near the ink of the Egna citation are slightly blurred but read as printed.
